It was followed by NICE-SLAM in December 2021 [S1].

NICE-SLAM is an improvement on iMAP that uses a hierarchical grid-based representation to fill gaps in large-scale unobserved scene features [S1].

The claim states that NICE-SLAM is an improvement on iMAP, uses a hierarchical grid-based representation, and fills gaps in large-scale unobserved scene features. The provided evidence explicitly states: 'Building on iMAP, NICE-SLAM... improved various aspects... Specifically, they used a hierarchical gridbased representation of the scene geometry, which was able to fill in gaps in iMAP reconstruction of large-scale unobserved scene features'. All facts in the claim are directly present in the evidence.

The evidence explicitly states that for iMAP, 'when combined with the much slower NeRF-based mapping step iMAP is far from achieving real-time performance.' It further notes that NICE-SLAM, despite optimizations, 'is still far from achieving real-time performance.' This confirms that the computational cost of the NeRF-based mapping step limits the overall performance (specifically regarding real-time capability).

The claim states that 'Pose tracking speed is close to camera framerate'. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states: 'iMAP achieved a pose tracking speed close to the camera framerate by running the much faster tracking step in parallel with the mapping process.' Since the claim is a direct restatement of a fact found in the evidence, the verdict is supported.
